This Mfa Is Filed U/S 173(1) Of Mv Act Against The
Judgment And Award Dated 27.03.2019 Passed In Mvc
No.507/2018 On The File Of The 5Th Additional District
And Sessions Judge, Additional Mact, Hassan, Partly
Allowing The Claim Petition For Compensation And
Seeking Enhancement Of Compensation.

This Appeal, Coming On For Further Orders, This
Day, Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice H.T. Narendra Prasad
 Oral Judgment
1.

This appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act')
has been filed by the claimant being aggrieved by the judgment dated 27.03.2019 passed by the 5th
Additional District and Sessions Judge, Hassan in Mvc No.507/2018.
2.

Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 03.07.2016, the claimant was traveling NC: 2024:KHC:31913 in the Car bearing Registration No.KA-46-M-3350 along with her parents near Naidupet-Putala Pattu National Highway near Diguva Chavali Village of Andrapradesh and at that time, the said Car was drove it in a rash and negligent manner and the accident had taken place due to the fault of the driver of the said Car.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the claimant sustained grievous injuries and was hospitalized.
3. The claimant filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act, seeking compensation.
It was pleaded that she spent significant amount towards medical expenses, conveyance charges and other related costs.
It was further pleaded that the accident occurred solely on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
4. Upon service of notice, the respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared through counsel and filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.

sentences.text:
On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter,
recorded the evidence.
The claimant, who is a minor, in order to prove the case, examined her mother as PW-1 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.P1 to Ex.P16.

On behalf of the respondents,
neither examined any witness nor exhibited any document.

The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment, inter alia, held that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver, as a result of which, the claimant sustained injuries.

The Tribunal further held that the claimant is entitled to a compensation of Rs.2,25,000/- along with interest at the rate of 9% p.a. and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved, the present appeal has been filed.
6. The learned counsel for the claimant has submitted that at the time of the accident, the claimant was a one- year-old baby.
According to the wound certificate, she NC: 2024:KHC:31913 sustained multiple abrasions all over her body, was unconscious, and suffered fractures to both parietal bones and the left temporal bone.
The injuries are grievous in nature, as evidenced by the Wound Certificate, Discharge Summary, and other medical records produced by the claimant.
These injuries will likely impact her future education.
She has suffered lot of pain during treatment.
Considering these factors, the global compensation of Rs.2,25,000/- awarded by the Tribunal appears inadequate.
Hence, he sought for allowing the appeal.
7. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the Insurance Company has submitted that the claimant, apart from producing medical records, did not examine the doctor as a witness.

Moreover,
it is not the claimant's case that the accidental injuries have hindered her ability to pursue her studies.
Therefore, it is evident that the injuries will not impede the claimant's further education.
Considering the evidence presented by both parties and the material on record, the Tribunal has awarded a just NC: 2024:KHC:31913 and reasonable compensation.

He further submitted that in light of the Division Bench decision of this Court in the case of Ms.Joyeeta Bose and others -v- Venkateshan.V and others (MFA 5896/2018 and connected matters disposed of on 24.8.2020), the rate of interest awarded by the Tribunal at 9% p.a. on the compensation amount appears excessive.

8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.
9.
It is not in dispute that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
10. At the time of the accident, the claimant was a one- year-old baby.
According to the wound certificate, she sustained multiple abrasions all over her body, was unconscious and suffered fractures to both parietal bones and the left temporal bone.

She has suffered lot of pain NC:

However, the claimant did not examine the doctor as a witness and no evidence was produced to show that she underwent surgery or that the injuries have affected her studies.

Considering the claimant's evidence and the nature of injuries mentioned in the wound Prajaktha P. Guptha vs Pruthvi S. Guptha on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54526703/
3 certificate and Discharge Summary, I am inclined to award an additional compensation of Rs.1,00,000/-, in addition to the compensation of Rs.2,25,000/- already awarded by the Tribunal.

sentences.text:
11. In the result, the following order is passed:
ORDER a) The appeal is allowed in part.
b) The judgment of the Claims Tribunal is modified.
c) The claimant is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.3,25,000/-.

d) Following the judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in the case of 'MS.JOYEETA BOSE' (supra), the enhanced compensation shall carry interest at 6%
per annum.

The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.

Sd/-
